newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine labor reform debate falters.
newsitem.headline: Argentine labor reform debate falters.

text.p: Argentine trade unions and business leaders said Thursday their contacts over labor reform plans had broken down and negotiations would have to continue in Congress.

President Carlos Menem has insisted labor reform is the only way to reduce hiring costs and reduce unemployment of 17.3 percent. He tried to push it through by decree, but was stymied by the courts, and then encouraged three-way talks with unions and business leaders, which have made little progress.

Businessmen say the government has now watered down its reform plans in a draft deal struck with the main trade union federation, the CGT, behind their backs. They are especially concerned about the government's preliminary deal with unions to drop plans to scrap collective wage deals and swap redundancy payouts for unemployment insurance schemes.
An official at the CGT told Reuters: "The CGT does not want to negotiate any more with the business sector, we believe these contacts are over."
"We want the discussion moved to Congress and the businessmen to express their views there, as the CGT will also."

On the employers' side, industrialist Francisco Macri said there were "two or three inflexible positions and no way of reaching an immediate agreement, so if the government has decided to move the debate to Congress, we'll continue there."
He described the union position as "a little rigid."
